Opening Hook

Imagine waking up at 3am with a racing heart. Your palms are sweaty and your mind is spinning through tomorrow's exam. That surge you feel is your stress response activating.

Discussion Questions

Q1
What distinguishes acute stress from chronic stress at the neurobiological level?
Teaching note: Prompt students to consider duration and habituation.
Q2
How does cortisol affect memory consolidation differently in the hippocampus versus the amygdala?
Teaching note: Pair-share before large group discussion.
Q3

Teaching note: Encourage examples from student life.

Quiz Items

Question 1
Which gland releases cortisol in response to ACTH?
  • A. Adrenal cortex
  • B. Anterior pituitary
  • C. Hypothalamus
  • D. Pineal gland
Answer: A • Rationale
The adrenal cortex (zona fasciculata) synthesizes and releases cortisol in response to ACTH from the anterior pituitary.
Question 2
Which of the following best describes negative feedback in the HPA axis?
  • A. Cortisol inhibits CRH and ACTH release
  • B. ACTH stimulates CRH production
  • C. Cortisol amplifies the stress response
  • D. CRH directly stimulates the adrenal gland
Answer: A • Rationale
Cortisol feeds back to inhibit both CRH from the hypothalamus and ACTH from the pituitary, forming a classic negative feedback loop.

Key Concepts

  • cortisol: primary glucocorticoid hormone secreted by the adrenal cortex during stress
  • HPA axis: hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis; the neuroendocrine pathway governing the stress response
  • CRH: corticotropin-releasing hormone released by the hypothalamus
  • ACTH: adrenocorticotropic hormone released by the pituitary
  • negative feedback: mechanism by which cortisol suppresses CRH and ACTH

Homework / Reflection

Over the next week, keep a brief stress diary. Each evening, note one stressful event, rate its intensity (1-10), and identify the physical and cognitive symptoms you noticed. Bring your diary to the next session.
